text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.7% today after crude oil prices dropped for a second consecutive day on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict. The stock had surged $4 over the previous two sessions as geopolitical tensions drove oil above $154, but those gains reversed as market sentiment shifted toward negotiation rather than escalation—crude is now down to $103 per barrel domestically.

The broader uncertainty heading into the midterm elections also likely weighed on energy stocks today. Political changes could reshape energy policy in ways that favor renewables over traditional oil production, adding another layer of concern for investors holding oil and gas companies.
